stories.title: Shane Steichen sticking with Daniel Jones as Colts' QB1 for Week 9 vs. Cowboys
stories.summary: Daniel Jones will remain the Colts' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
stories.detail: INDIANAPOLIS -- Daniel Jones remains the Colts ' QB1. Coach Shane Steichen on Monday said Jones will remain the Colts' starting quarterback for the team's Week 9 game against the Dallas Cowboys despite leaving the door open to a change after the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards against Jacksonville (5.1 yards per attempt), throwing two more interceptions to raise his season total to nine picks. One of the interceptions came on a dropped pass by tight end Tyler Warren , resulting in a pick-six touchdown for the Jaguars. The Colts' offense ranks among the worst in the NFL in many major categories, including offensive expected points added (31st). Personally, Jones has ranked as one of the worst quarterbacks this season in QBR. His 39.6 QBR is the second worst he has produced in his eight seasons. But Steichen warned that the issues plaguing the Colts' offense are bigger than Jones. "Evaluating the tape, looking back at it, some things he could do better, some things that we need to help him with moving forward," Steichen said. "But I do feel that Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now." After Sunday's gam…

stories.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires Drew Rosenhaus as agent, eyes return to NFL
stories.summary: Brandon Aiyuk has hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that he is "working on getting him back to work and playing again in the NFL."
stories.detail: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Estranged San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has hired Drew Rosenhaus to represent him, the agent told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday. Rosenhaus told Schefter that he is "working on getting [Aiyuk] back to work and playing again in the NFL." Aiyuk has not played in an NFL game since Oct. 20, 2024, against the Kansas City Chiefs , when he tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee. For most of the time since, Aiyuk and the Niners have been at odds. The team placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left squad list in December after Aiyuk stopped showing up at the team facility. That came on the heels of the Niners voiding roughly $27 million in guaranteed money on Aiyuk's contract in July 2025 because he did not do the requisite rehab sessions and check-ins with the team during that offseason. When Aiyuk did not report for training camp in July, he reverted to the reserve/did not report list. For Aiyuk to play again, he must first apply for reinstatement with the NFL. If he does that, the Niners will then need to decide what to do with his rights. San Francisco has tried unsuccessfully to trade Aiyuk in the past, but if he's reinstated, the more likely o…

stories.title: Seahawks activate Jadarian Price from IR
stories.summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald didn't commit to playing running back Jadarian Price against the Bears when he was asked about it on Saturday, but it looks like the rookie will be back in the lineup.
stories.detail: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald didn’t commit to playing running back Jadarian Price against the Bears when he was asked about it on Saturday, but it looks like the rookie will be back in the lineup. Price was activated from injured reserve on Monday afternoon and he had no injury designation for the game, so it would appear he'll be active for the first time since Week 3. Price has been sidelined by a chest injury. The Seahawks could also welcome Zach Charbonnet back to the backfield on Monday night. He was activated in Week 7, but did not play in Seattle's win over the Chiefs. Running back Robert Henry was waived to open a spot for Price, which leaves Emanuel Wilson, George Holani and Velus Jones to go with Price and Charbonnet. The Seahawks also elevated wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr. and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed and left tackle Charles Cross have both been ruled out for the matchup with the Bears.

stories.title: Vikings uncertain of QB Kyler Murray's status vs. Bills due to sore hamstring
stories.summary: Vikings QB Kyler Murray's status for the Week 9 game against the Bills is uncertain due to a sore hamstring.
stories.detail: EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray 's hamstring was sore enough Monday that the team is uncertain whether he will be available for the team's Week 9 game against the Buffalo Bills . A day after Murray struggled in a 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions , coach Kevin O'Connell said that Murray was going through a "full eval" Monday and that he expected additional updates from the Vikings' medical staff during the early part of the week. Asked if he thought the injury was serious enough to prevent Murray from playing against the Bills, O'Connell said: "I don't think we're there yet. It's still early enough that I'll continue to get updates." If Murray can't play, backup Carson Wentz would make his second start of the season. O'Connell, however, made clear that he is not considering benching Murray for performance reasons. Through his first six starts with the Vikings, Murray ranks No. 26 among 30 qualified quarterbacks in QBR. But when asked if Murray would continue to be his starter when healthy, O'Connell said: "Yes." stories.title: Chiefs' Reid says he didn't bench OL Suamataia as punishment
stories.summary: Chiefs coach Andy Reid explained Monday that his decision to bench left guard Kingsley Suamataia for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos was not punishment toward the three-year player.
stories.detail: DENVER -- Chiefs coach Andy Reid explained Monday that his decision to bench left guard Kingsley Suamataia for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos was not punishment toward the three-year player. "This is just between Kingsley and I," Reid said, reiterating what he said after the Chiefs' 28-24 loss. "It's not something that's earth shattering. I'll just keep it there." Prior to Sunday's game, Suamataia was a full participant in the Chiefs' three practices last week and wasn't on the team's injury report. But during the team's pregame warmup, backup guard Mike Caliendo , a four-year veteran, took most of the reps at left guard with the rest of the starting offensive line. Caliendo played all 69 of the Chiefs' offensive snaps while Suamataia was on the field for just five snaps on special teams. Without Suamataia, the 2024 second-round pick, the Chiefs didn't have much success running the ball against the Broncos. Running back Kenneth Walker III finished with just 69 rushing yards on 21 attempts. stories.title: Wilbon taking leave of absence from ESPN to address health issues
stories.summary: Michael Wilbon, the longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of "Pardon the Interruption," is taking a leave of absence to address health issues.
stories.detail: Michael Wilbon is taking a break. The longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of the network's popular "Pardon the Interruption" talk show alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced Monday that he is taking a leave of absence because of what he described as "multiple health issues." Wilbon, who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to "the injured list" but added that he hopes it is "not an extended one." While Wilbon, who is also featured on ESPN's NBA coverage, declined to go into detail about what he is facing, he added that there are people in his personal life who noticed "worrisome signs" in recent years that he largely ignored. Wilbon did make a point to note the issues are not alcohol- or gambling-related. "I have no idea how exactly this part of my journey will wind up," Wilbon posted. "The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony." Wilbon's last appearance on "PTI," which recently celebrated its 25th anniversary and is credited with revolutionizing television's "sports debate" format, was Oct. 26. The show, in part, is a byproduct of the friendship of Wilbon and Kornheiser,…

stories.title: Thunder to retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0
stories.summary: The Thunder will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 this season. The former MVP played the first 11 of his 18 seasons in Oklahoma City.
stories.detail: The Oklahoma City Thunder announced they will retire Russell Westbrook 's No. 0 in the rafters on Feb. 7. Westbrook was a first-round pick of the organization in 2008, just days before the team officially became the Thunder after relocating from Seattle. Westbrook played the first 11 years of his 18-season career in OKC and paired with Kevin Durant to turn the young Thunder into one of the best teams in the league. However, after Durant's free agent departure following the 2015-16 season, Westbrook's stature in Oklahoma City grew. The next season, Westbrook became the first player to average a triple-double for an entire season since Oscar Robertson, going for 31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists, and was named league MVP. He continued to average a triple-double for the following two seasons, his final ones with the Thunder. "Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," Thunder executive vice president and general manager Sam Presti said in a statement Monday. teamStories.detail: Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season . After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as: The sky is falling in Oklahoma City , New York and Miami ! The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go! Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball ! Ty Jerome ? Ty Jerome! With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. ( Note: stats through Tuesday's games .) The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008. Zach Kram: Not an overreaction For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft. Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve.
